clue.text: Middle East food, some not entirely in season in Georgia

indicators.note: in says one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: in the American state of Georgia autumn is called fall

indicators.note: not entirely tells us to drop the last letter of the phrase for some

parts.note: some means a few

explanation.surface: A description of a snack eaten in Georgia when the weather is turning, more or less.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in Georgia' marks the season as the American word for autumn; 'not entirely' trims a few to AFE.
explanation.definitionFit: Deep-fried chickpea balls are a staple street snack across the Levant and wider Arab world.

clue.text: Account in decline, deceptive appearance

indicators.note: in says the abbreviation sits inside the other word

parts.note: to decline is to fade away

explanation.surface: A bank account going downhill while everything looks fine on the outside.
explanation.definitionFit: A façade is literally a building's front, figuratively an outward show hiding the truth.

clue.text: Electrified track is uniform

parts.note: an electrified wire or rail is live
RY is an abbreviation for railway, a track

explanation.surface: A railway announcement that the electrified track is standard throughout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uniform' looks like an adjective meaning consistent but is the noun: an outfit.
explanation.definitionFit: Livery is the distinctive uniform worn by servants or members of a guild, a noun synonym.

clue.text: Threatening, in order to obtain invitation

parts.note: for has this sense, as in 'go out for milk'
a bidding is an invitation or summons

explanation.surface: Someone is being menacing just to get themselves invited.
explanation.definitionFit: Forbidding describes something grim and unwelcoming in look, synonymous with threatening or ominous.

clue.text: Deceitful, doing well to skim off capital

indicators.note: skimming off the capital means removing the first letter

parts.note: someone doing well is flying

explanation.surface: A crooked financier, thriving by siphoning off money from a fund.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' looks financial but means the first letter, the F of FLYING.
explanation.definitionFit: Lying means telling untruths, so a lying person is dishonest and deceitful.

clue.text: Guy carrying container of beer back in hamper

indicators.note: carrying says the guy holds the other piece inside him

parts.note: a guy is a man, a male

indicators.note: back says the container word is turned round to read the other way

parts.note: beer comes in a can

explanation.surface: A man lugging a beer can back inside a picnic hamper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns the can round to NAC, and 'carrying' holds it. 'hamper' looks like a picnic basket but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To hamper someone is to restrict their movement, as handcuffs or shackles do; synonym as verbs.

clue.text: Thus one is up to describe reptile in millimetres as a small version

indicators.note: in says the whole assembly sits inside the abbreviation

parts.note: mm is the abbreviation for millimetres

indicators.note: to describe is to draw round, so one piece encloses the other
in a down entry, up says the words for thus and one are read from bottom to top

parts.note: thus means so
the Roman numeral for one is I
a croc is short for a crocodile, a reptile

explanation.surface: A tiny model of a crocodile, drawn so small it is measured in millimetres.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is up' turns thus-plus-one to IOS, as this is a down entry; 'to describe' means to draw round, and 'in' sets everything between the two Ms.
explanation.definitionFit: A microcosm is a world in miniature, something reproducing the features of a larger whole on a small scale.

clue.text: Square in town in England

indicators.note: the first in says the answer lies within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A town square somewhere in England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Square' looks like a town square but means a square number.
explanation.definitionFit: Nine is three times three, a square number in arithmetic.

clue.text: See 15
Flat, then something ebbing and flowing late in the day

parts.note: a flat surface is even
the sea's tide ebbs and flows

explanation.surface: A calm sea, then the tide going in and out as evening comes on.
explanation.definitionFit: Eventide is a poetic word for evening, the late part of the day.

clue.text: Fielder caught a few balls

parts.note: C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
an over in cricket is a set of six balls bowled

explanation.surface: A cricket fielder took a catch after only a handful of deliveries.
explanation.definitionFit: Cover is a fielding position in cricket, on the off side, and by extension the player stationed there.

clue.text: Carrot in a piece of American bread I have for afters

parts.note: bread is slang for money; a cent is a US coin
I have contracts to I've

explanation.surface: A carrot sitting inside a slice of American bread, with dessert to follow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bread' is slang for money, so the 'piece' is a coin.
explanation.definitionFit: A carrot dangled in front of someone is an inducement or reward that motivates them.

clue.text: 26 character, a heavy weight to his lover?

definitions.note: a character created by the author at 26 across

parts.note: a lover might be called his darling
a ton is a large unit of weight

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a hefty sweetheart is a burden to her man.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord Darlington is a character in Wilde's play Lady Windermere's Fan.
explanation.definitionFit: Lord Darlington is the dandy who tempts the heroine in Wilde's play Lady Windermere's Fan.

clue.text: Amendment finally in place, so keep the original text

indicators.note: in says the letter goes inside the other piece

parts.note: to place something is to set it down

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of the word Amendment

explanation.surface: An editor, after an amendment is made, decides the original wording should stand.
explanation.definitionFit: Proofreaders write this Latin word, meaning 'let it stand', to cancel a correction and restore the original wording.

clue.text: Strength in a stable marriage never ends, hope rows frivolous?

indicators.note: frivolous means silly and unsettled, so those letters are muddled
ends picks the closing letter of each of marriage and never

explanation.surface: Musings on whether a solid marriage lasts, or whether hopes and quarrels are just silly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ends' takes E and R from marriage and never; 'frivolous' mixes them with HOPE ROWS. 'stable' suggests steady wedlock but is a horses' stable.
explanation.definitionFit: Horsepower is a unit of engine power, and playfully the power of animals kept in a stable.

clue.text: Shamed, the Guardian boss is paying for our food?

parts.note: a dish is a serving of food
'it's on me' means I am paying for it
taken as written
ED is short for editor, the boss of a newspaper like the Guardian

explanation.surface: Is the newspaper's editor picking up the bill for our lunch, to our embarrassment?
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces run in a different order from the clue: the boss (ED) is the one who goes on our dish, so ED comes last.
explanation.definitionFit: Shamed and disgraced are synonyms, both describing someone brought into public discredit.

clue.text: Short in credit briefly, terrible fraud, 26 character

definitions.note: a character created by the author at 26 across

indicators.note: fraud suggests something fake, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: CR is the abbreviation for credit

explanation.surface: Someone short of credit for a while commits a dreadful fraud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fraud' rearranges SHORT IN CR TERRIBLE. Sir Robert Chiltern is the politician with a guilty secret in Wilde's An Ideal Husband.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Robert Chiltern is the compromised politician at the centre of Wilde's play An Ideal Husband.

clue.text: Plague half contained in saga

indicators.note: contained in says one piece sits within the other

parts.note: a saga is a long epic
demi- is a prefix meaning half

explanation.surface: A plague that takes up half of a long tale.
explanation.definitionFit: An epidemic is a widespread outbreak of disease, which is what a plague is.

clue.text: Heinous crime no longer naff for 26 character

definitions.note: a character created by the author at 26 across

indicators.note: heinous means atrocious, signalling the letters are mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: A dreadful offence that is now considered fashionable after all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heinous' rearranges CRIME NO LONGER NAFF. Algernon Moncrieff is Jack's witty friend in The Importance of Being Earnest; 'naff' is British slang for uncool.
explanation.definitionFit: Algernon Moncrieff is the dandy friend who invents Bunbury in Wilde's The Importance of Being Earnest.

clue.text: God's dog and ten animals I slam in a net, perhaps?

definitions.text: God's dog and ten animals I slam in a net, perhaps?

parts.words: God's dog and ten animals I slam in a net, perhaps?
parts.note: both phrases read the same letter by letter backwards as forwards, so they are examples of word games of that kind

explanation.walkthrough: Spell 'God's dog' or 'ten animals I slam in a net' backwards and you get the same letters; 'perhaps' marks them as examples.
explanation.definitionFit: Words or phrases reading the same in both directions are the type of wordplay shown by the two examples.

clue.text: Breather, that is, for Scottish servant

parts.note: a gill is the organ a fish breathes through
ie is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A Scottish servant is allowed a short rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Breather' suggests a rest but means the organ a fish breathes through.
explanation.definitionFit: A gillie is a Highland attendant who helps on fishing or deer-stalking outings; a Scottish word.

clue.text: Coin in hole

parts.note: a vent is a hole or opening

explanation.surface: A coin dropped into a slot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coin' looks like money but is the verb, as in coining a phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: To coin a word or phrase is to devise it fresh, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Does dingo eat enormous radishes for starters?

definitions.note: a plural noun defining a plural noun is fair: does are several female animals, and the answer word serves as its own plural

indicators.note: for starters asks for the opening letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: A whimsical question about whether a wild Australian dog snacks on giant vegetables.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Does' reads as a verb opening a question, but it is the plural of doe.
explanation.definitionFit: A doe is a female of several animal species, most familiarly the female of the antlered woodland animal.

clue.text: Immorality in trio up for rolling round in cheese

indicators.note: the second in places the shuffled letters inside the other piece

parts.note: cheese in the sense of trite, sentimental stuff is corn, as in corny

indicators.note: rolling round suggests tumbling the letters of trio up into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Something wicked going on with three people rolling about in a cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rolling round' gives RUPTIO and 'in' houses it. 'cheese' looks like food but means corniness: trite, sentimental stuff.
explanation.definitionFit: Corruption is moral decay or depravity, a close synonym of wickedness and vice.

clue.text: Arm uprooting the Spanish tree

indicators.note: uprooting a tree turns it bottom up, so in a down entry the pieces read upwards

parts.note: el is Spanish for the
a fir is a conifer tree

explanation.surface: A Spanish tree torn up by an arm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arm' looks like a limb but means a weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: A rifle is a firearm, and arms are weapons, so the singular noun fits.

clue.text: £0.00 charge — about right?

indicators.note: about says one piece goes around the other

parts.note: a fee is a charge

explanation.surface: A price tag of nothing: is that a fair fee?
explanation.definitionFit: Something costing nothing at all is complimentary or gratis, priced at zero pounds.

clue.text: See 17
Penning the ultimate in drivel, yawning author

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: a yawning gap is a wide one

indicators.note: the ultimate in picks the final letter of the word drivel

explanation.surface: A bored writer, yawning as he churns out the last of his rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Penning' looks like writing but means enclosing: WIDE holds L.
explanation.definitionFit: Oscar Wilde was the Irish playwright and wit, writer of the play that runs through this puzzle.

clue.text: Party issued approval

parts.note: Con is the abbreviation for the Conservative party
issued means sent out

explanation.surface: A political party has given official sign-off.
explanation.definitionFit: Consent is permission or agreement, so it is a synonym of approval.

clue.text: Serious attention given to home

parts.note: to give someone your ear is to pay attention
a nest is a bird's home

explanation.surface: Someone gives proper, serious thought to their home.
explanation.walkthrough: Also the theme: Wilde's The Importance of Being Earnest.
explanation.definitionFit: Earnest describes someone sincere and grave in intent, a straightforward synonym of serious.
